chapter: Royal Roost, Birdland and Three O'Clock High
title: Royal Roost: drugs, the band and Miles Davis sitting in
summary: Collins describes the junkie culture at the Royal Roost, the dealer who sat with the band, and Miles Davis playing nightly without pay.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah, I think it was -- I think it was Metronome. Yeah, that record -- yeah, it's a very good record. But any way, the Royal Roost. Everybody was a junkie. I would go to work, and keep my coat, my overcoat right next to me, you know, I mean right on the stand I would
just put it , because as soon as we finished playing I would walk outside because I was afraid the band was going to be busted. It was freezing outside.

But the man would come to work with us, I mean the man who sold the dope, he came to work. It was a regular job with him, he came and sat right beside the band and so he furnished the band with dope, you know. But a great band. But at this time -- let's see, I'll tell you. Miles, who at that time -- I don't think Miles even drank beer. Miles -- Tad didn't offer Miles enough money, so Miles wouldn't accept a job, but he came and played with us every night. But this is the truth. Tad was paying the band out of his pocket, you know, because nobody would work for scale. He had everybody, you know, like Kenny Clark on drums, Cecil Payne, J. J., you know, I mean it was a tremendous band.
